intro: These are mountaineering clubs and organisations from different regions. Locations are shown at city level. Click a marker or a card to see details, or allow your location to see how far each one is from you.

clubs.name: The Alpine Club
clubs.focus: Oldest mountaineering club in the world. Meets, library and archive, and the Alpine Journal.

clubs.name: Swiss Alpine Club (SAC)
clubs.focus: A national club that runs a large network of mountain huts across the Swiss Alps.

clubs.name: Club Alpino Italiano (CAI)
clubs.focus: Italy's national mountaineering club, founded in Turin. Maintains hundreds of huts and paths.

clubs.name: Deutscher Alpenverein (DAV)
clubs.focus: One of the largest mountaineering associations in the world, with over a million members.

clubs.name: FFCAM (Club Alpin Français)
clubs.focus: The French mountaineering and climbing federation, with huts around Chamonix and the Écrins.

clubs.name: American Alpine Club
clubs.focus: Publishes the American Alpine Journal and gives grants for climbing expeditions.

clubs.name: Alpine Club of Canada
clubs.focus: Runs backcountry huts and training courses in the Canadian Rockies.

clubs.name: Alpine Ascents International
clubs.focus: A guiding company that leads climbs on Rainier, Denali, Aconcagua, Kilimanjaro and Everest.

clubs.name: Club Andino Boliviano
clubs.focus: Bolivia's mountaineering club, based in La Paz at around 3,600 m, close to the high Andes.

clubs.name: Nepal Mountaineering Association
clubs.focus: Represents Nepali mountaineering and issues permits for the trekking peaks.

clubs.name: Himalayan Mountaineering Institute
clubs.focus: Founded after the 1953 Everest climb, with Tenzing Norgay as its first director of field training.

clubs.name: Indian Mountaineering Foundation
clubs.focus: The national body for mountaineering in India. Organises expeditions and handles peak permits.

clubs.name: Japanese Alpine Club
clubs.focus: One of Asia's oldest alpine clubs. Japanese teams have a long record in the Himalaya.

clubs.name: Alpine Club of Pakistan
clubs.focus: Supports climbing in the Karakoram, home to K2 and three other 8,000 m peaks.

clubs.name: Mountain Club of South Africa
clubs.focus: Climbing, hiking and mountain rescue around Table Mountain and the Drakensberg.

clubs.name: Mountain Club of Kenya
clubs.focus: Climbs on Mount Kenya, Kilimanjaro and Rift Valley crags.

clubs.name: New Zealand Alpine Club
clubs.focus: Backcountry huts and mountaineering in the Southern Alps, the training ground of Edmund Hillary.
